result: For the nonnegative weighted grid R_w and projection chart in frontier-20261028-grid-weighted-entire-plane-v1.json SHA256 8a11286f1ec96cded986ef93d306791153dc1ace9ff601a12fdc2c83cab3f61b, mixing its two exact rank2 phase decompositions yields a joint 4x4 Gram criterion strictly stronger than applying either endpoint alone. A concrete PPT/SN3 4x5 source and actual PPT/SN2 4x4 projection satisfy the mixed criterion although both endpoint Grams fail. This is a written construction for a proper family, not a global 4x4 result.
definitions: Let R_w=alpha[A]+beta[B]+delta[D]+gamma[C]+epsilon[E]+phi[F]+eta[G]+iota[I]+kappa[H], using the source vectors and projection K3=v0|0>+v2|2>, K4=|3> from the cited artifact. Assume alpha,beta,epsilon,phi,eta,iota>0 and beta*delta>=alpha^2. Put k=sqrt(alpha^3)/beta, U=|v0|^2,V=|v2|^2>0, and D0=diag(epsilon,eta,iota,phi). Define t1(s)=(-(k+s*v0),(k+s*v0)*v0,(k+s*v0)*v2,s) and t2=(-v0/v2,v0^2/v2,v0,1/v2).
mixed_gram: For any real p in [0,1] and complex s, use fraction p of the first exact four-phase rank2 decomposition, and fraction 1-p of the second decomposition (one rank2 q0 plus four rank2 phase vectors), as displayed in the cited artifact. Both consume alpha[A']+beta[B']+(alpha^2/beta)[D']; their extra rank2-accounting terms are [W_s] with coefficient t1(s), and alpha[|22>] with coefficient t2. The residual is (delta-alpha^2/beta)[D']+gamma[C']+kappa[H'] plus the Gram H(p,s)=D0-p*t1*t1^*-(1-p)*alpha*t2*t2^* over (E',G',I',F'). Since the latter span has support on Alice rows2,3, H(p,s)>=0 implies an explicit SR<=2 decomposition. This remains true for p=0 or1; V=0 can be handled by the first phase certificate.
two_by_two_criterion: Since D0>0, put A1=t1^*D0^(-1)t1, A2=alpha*t2^*D0^(-1)t2, and Xi=alpha*|t1^*D0^(-1)t2|^2. The rank-two-update Schur complement gives H(p,s)>=0 iff 1-p*A1>=0, 1-(1-p)*A2>=0, and (1-p*A1)*(1-(1-p)*A2)-p*(1-p)*Xi>=0. The criterion is exact for this Gram mixture; it is only sufficient for SN<=2.
explicit_actual_state: Take source weights (alpha,beta,delta,gamma,epsilon,phi,eta,iota,kappa)=(1,1,2,3,9,9,9,1/10,100) and v0=0,v2=8/25, p=1/2,s=0. The all-plane sufficient weight condition from the cited artifact fails: k^2*(1/epsilon+alpha/(phi*iota))=11/9>1. Indeed the first endpoint cost is 1277/1125>1 and the second endpoint cost is 625/576>1, so neither endpoint Gram is PSD. The mixed Gram nonetheless has exact positive pivots [17/2,9,973/21250,527/128], and all 256 entries match the actual projected operator. Its actual partial transpose is PSD.
source_and_entanglement: All source weights are positive and an exact 20x20 partial-transpose calculation shows R_w>=0 and R_w^Gamma>=0; its trace is 1511/10. Its source range is the same nine-dimensional grid range whose corrected minors force the A coefficient of every SR<=2 range vector to vanish, while alpha>0, so R_w has SN>=3; the defining sum gives SN<=3. The projected state is entangled: its 3x3 core rank-one minors give 2a^2=-v2*a*f for every product vector in the actual range. Any separable decomposition would have sum|a|^2=alpha and sum|f|^2=phi, so Cauchy-Schwarz requires 4*alpha<=phi*V. Here phi*V=576/625<4=4*alpha. The exact mixed SR2 decomposition therefore proves SN exactly2 for the projected state.
ppt_simplification_of_predecessor: If R_w itself is PPT, the PT principal submatrices at |01>,|10>; |11>,|20>; and |23>,|30> imply beta*delta>=alpha^2, alpha*epsilon>=delta^2, and phi*eta>=epsilon^2. Hence epsilon>=alpha^3/beta^2=k^2 and phi*eta>=k^2*epsilon. Thus, on this PPT source family, the second weight inequality of the predecessor is automatic: its entire-plane theorem only needs the additional explicit sufficient condition k^2*(1/epsilon+alpha/(phi*iota))<=1. The example above shows that this sufficient condition and the two endpoint certificates are not necessary even for a particular PPT/SN2 output.

exact_check.observed: Gaussian Fraction arithmetic checks the nine phase-vector rank minors, all 256 entries of the actual mixed decomposition, mixed Gram pivots above, source 20x20 PT pivots and projected 16x16 PT pivots; it also hash-pins and replays five prior checker cases. The two endpoint costs and the source trace are exact. Universal p,s validity follows from the written phase identity and Gram Schur argument.

limits: Only the stated weighted grid and the K3-head/K4-tail chart are covered. The two-by-two test is not a necessary SN criterion, and the example's missing two endpoint certificates do not establish any higher Schmidt number. Entire-plane coverage for all weighted PPT sources, generic CP^4 kernels, a 4x4 SN>=3 target witness, independent/formal review and novelty remain open.
